fish.PolarCod.name: Polar cod
fish.PolarCod.description: Boreogadus saida. A small fish associated with cold Arctic waters.
fish.AtlanticCod.name: Atlantic cod
fish.AtlanticCod.description: Gadus morhua. A demersal fish of North Atlantic and adjacent waters.
fish.Capelin.name: Capelin
fish.Capelin.description: Mallotus villosus. A small schooling fish in northern seas.
fish.ArcticChar.name: Arctic char
fish.ArcticChar.description: Salvelinus alpinus. Lives in fresh water; some populations migrate to the sea.
fish.Halibut.name: Greenland halibut
fish.Halibut.description: Reinhardtius hippoglossoides. A deep-water flatfish; available only on the offshore route.
fish.Wolffish.name: Atlantic wolffish
fish.Wolffish.description: Anarhichas lupus. A bottom-dwelling fish associated with rocky habitats.
fish.GoldenRedfish.name: Golden redfish
fish.GoldenRedfish.description: Sebastes norvegicus. An orange-red deep-water North Atlantic fish; found on the offshore route.
receipt.name: Harbor order receipt
receipt.desc: Payment was added to your wallet. Keep as a souvenir or discard.
dialogue.Ada.Mon: The tide board is the first thing I check each morning.
dialogue.Ada.Tue: A small catch handled well is worth more than a crate left warm.
dialogue.Ada.Wed: The order board pays directly. Read which species is needed.
dialogue.Ada.Thu: Willy says you know how to be patient with a fishing rod.
dialogue.Ada.Fri: Our harbor is small. Everyone knows when a boat is late.
dialogue.Ada.Sat: Capelin arrive in schools. The gulls often notice first.
dialogue.Ada.Mon2: The blue building is our fishery. Come in out of the wind.
dialogue.Ada.Tue2: A good crate needs drainage and a clear label.
dialogue.Ada.Wed2: Roan repairs what the salt wears down. It is endless work.
dialogue.Ada.Thu2: There is no prize for landing more than you can handle.
dialogue.Ada.Fri2: We keep the deep-water route separate from the harbor.
dialogue.Ada.Sat2: Your first order does not expire. Take your time.
dialogue.Ada.Sun2: A clean worktable is a useful kind of luxury.
dialogue.Ada.Mon4: I keep the old shipping ledgers. They tell quite a story.
dialogue.Ada.Tue4: Not every northern town catches the same species.
dialogue.Ada.Wed4: I like an orderly morning and an unhurried supper.
dialogue.Ada.Thu4: The first crate of the season always feels special.
dialogue.Ada.Fri4: Thanks for bringing your catch in carefully.
dialogue.Ada.Sat4: You have made yourself part of this harbor.
dialogue.Ada.intro: I am Ada. Welcome to Frosthavn.
dialogue.Ada.rain: Come inside. Work can wait until the weather settles.
dialogue.Ada.winter: The snow makes the harbor quiet. The sea is still working.
gift.Ada.love: That is very thoughtful. Thank you!
gift.Ada.like: I can make good use of this.
gift.Ada.dislike: I do not have much use for this.
gift.Ada.hate: Please keep that away from the workbench.
gift.Ada.neutral: Thank you for thinking of me.
dialogue.Mira.Mon: Check the route before you check the clock.
dialogue.Mira.Tue: Sea ice can look solid from a distance. We stay on shore.
dialogue.Mira.Wed: My dogs each have their own pace. A team learns to listen.
dialogue.Mira.Thu: Summer tundra is not a forest hiding under snow.
dialogue.Mira.Fri: Those low plants grow slowly. Stay on the marked path.
dialogue.Mira.Sat: For a winter journey, check the equipment notes at our tundra stop.
dialogue.Mira.Sun: Wild bears need distance, never food from our hands.
dialogue.Mira.Mon2: I like the sound of boots on packed snow.
dialogue.Mira.Tue2: A good guide knows when to turn back.
dialogue.Mira.Wed2: A sheltered place to rest is part of a good route.
dialogue.Mira.Thu2: The river belongs to the char before it belongs to our maps.
dialogue.Mira.Fri2: You can watch a fox without following it.
dialogue.Mira.Sat2: The hills are quiet today. That does not mean empty.
dialogue.Mira.Sun2: I mend a strap before it breaks.
dialogue.Mira.Mon4: Snow houses are seasonal shelters, not every northern home.
dialogue.Mira.Tue4: A bright summer night can make bedtime easy to forget.
dialogue.Mira.Wed4: The path north takes you onto the tundra.
dialogue.Mira.Thu4: We return with the same team we set out with.
dialogue.Mira.Fri4: A warm drink is even better after a careful journey.
dialogue.Mira.Sat4: You have learned to look before you hurry.
dialogue.Mira.intro: I am Mira. Welcome to Frosthavn.
dialogue.Mira.rain: Come inside. Work can wait until the weather settles.
dialogue.Mira.winter: The snow makes the harbor quiet. The sea is still working.
gift.Mira.love: That is very thoughtful. Thank you!
gift.Mira.like: I can make good use of this.
gift.Mira.dislike: I do not have much use for this.
gift.Mira.hate: Please keep that away from the workbench.
gift.Mira.neutral: Thank you for thinking of me.
dialogue.Roan.Mon: Salt finds every screw I forget to grease.
dialogue.Roan.Tue: I am fixing the processing shed, one board at a time.
dialogue.Roan.Wed: Bring the materials to me, not to the order board.
dialogue.Roan.Thu: A boat is a collection of small jobs done properly.
dialogue.Roan.Fri: That old hull still has good years in it.
dialogue.Roan.Sat: We only open the fjord route after the repairs.
dialogue.Roan.Sun: Willy once sent me a box of spare fittings. Useful fellow.
dialogue.Roan.Mon2: The smoker needs coal. Good fish deserves careful processing.
dialogue.Roan.Tue2: I wrote the measurement down. Somewhere very sensible.
dialogue.Roan.Wed2: A dry pair of gloves saves a surprising amount of trouble.
dialogue.Roan.Thu2: Icebergs are scenery, not stepping stones.
dialogue.Roan.Fri2: The pier rail is there for a reason.
dialogue.Roan.Sat2: I prefer repairing things to throwing them away.
dialogue.Roan.Sun2: The yellow house catches the afternoon light nicely.
dialogue.Roan.Mon4: When the wind rises, the workbench can wait.
dialogue.Roan.Tue4: A small leak gets a large note in my book.
dialogue.Roan.Wed4: I am proud of this little harbor.
dialogue.Roan.Thu4: Thank you for lending a hand with the first shipment.
dialogue.Roan.Fri4: The fjord is deeper than it looks from the landing.
dialogue.Roan.Sat4: There is always another hinge to oil tomorrow.

dialogue.Roan.rain: Come inside. Work can wait until the weather settles.

gift.Roan.like: I can make good use of this.
gift.Roan.dislike: I do not have much use for this.
gift.Roan.hate: Please keep that away from the workbench.
gift.Roan.neutral: Thank you for thinking of me.
dialogue.Nora.Mon: I keep the wind chart where spray cannot reach it.
dialogue.Nora.Tue: The flag at the strip tells more than the clouds do.
dialogue.Nora.Wed: A clear runway is a working surface, not a footpath.
dialogue.Nora.Thu: If the fjord wind turns, we wait before we fly.
dialogue.Nora.Fri: The horizon stays bright long after the sun slips away.
dialogue.Nora.Sat: I mark visibility from the same lookout each morning.
dialogue.Nora.Sun: A calm harbor does not promise calm weather inland.
dialogue.Nora.Mon2: The little vane needs oil before the first frost.
dialogue.Nora.Tue2: I would rather delay a flight than guess at the cloud base.
dialogue.Nora.Wed2: Snow crystals gather on the windward side of every post.
dialogue.Nora.Thu2: Keep your gloves dry; cold hands read a chart poorly.
dialogue.Nora.Fri2: That blue line is yesterday’s sea-ice edge, not a route.
dialogue.Nora.Sat2: We compare notes before we call a day settled.
dialogue.Nora.Sun2: There is no prize for being first into a headwind.
dialogue.Nora.Mon4: I like the small silence just before snow begins.
dialogue.Nora.Tue4: The radio check is short: signal, position, return plan.
dialogue.Nora.Wed4: A thin strip of open water can change the whole forecast.
dialogue.Nora.Thu4: The lamps guide arrivals; they never replace a weather check.
dialogue.Nora.Fri4: Thank you for helping keep the route notes current.
dialogue.Nora.Sat4: Tomorrow’s chart begins with what we actually saw today.

dialogue.Levin.Mon: A field note needs a place, a time and what you really saw.
dialogue.Levin.Tue: I leave the stones where the meltwater carried them.
dialogue.Levin.Wed: The tundra is low and patient, not an empty lawn.
dialogue.Levin.Thu: A fish from the stream tells a different story from a sea catch.
dialogue.Levin.Fri: I sketch the ice edge from solid ground.
dialogue.Levin.Sat: Fox tracks can cross an old path without ever meeting us.
dialogue.Levin.Sun: A seal at the waterline needs room to leave.
dialogue.Levin.Mon2: I never collect a sample without writing down why.
dialogue.Levin.Tue2: The glacier changes slowly enough to fool a hurried eye.
dialogue.Levin.Wed2: Moss grows low because the wind has the last word here.
dialogue.Levin.Thu2: A clear photograph can be better evidence than a souvenir.
dialogue.Levin.Fri2: We record an uncertain sighting as uncertain.
dialogue.Levin.Sat2: The fjord carries sound farther than you expect.
dialogue.Levin.Sun2: A dark patch in the water is not automatically an animal.
dialogue.Levin.Mon4: I label every sample before it leaves the field kit.
dialogue.Levin.Tue4: Short plants have short growing seasons to work with.
dialogue.Levin.Wed4: The best observation often begins by standing still.
dialogue.Levin.Thu4: Thank you for bringing the receipt and the specimen notes.
dialogue.Levin.Fri4: The research hut is warm enough for a careful drawing.
dialogue.Levin.Sat4: Good records leave space for the next person to learn.

dialogue.Amma.Mon: Every dog has a different stride; I match the team to the trail.
dialogue.Amma.Tue: We check every buckle before we leave the camp.
dialogue.Amma.Wed: The dogs get water before they get a treat.
dialogue.Amma.Thu: A steady pace keeps the whole team together.
dialogue.Amma.Fri: I brush packed snow from the harness after each run.
dialogue.Amma.Sat: We turn back when the trail markers disappear.
dialogue.Amma.Sun: A warm paw check is part of the evening routine.
dialogue.Amma.Mon2: The sled runners need a smooth edge, not a sharp one.
dialogue.Amma.Tue2: I never tie a team where a loose line can cross a path.
dialogue.Amma.Wed2: The dogs know the camp by its sounds and smells.
dialogue.Amma.Thu2: A quiet dog can still be tired; watch the whole team.
dialogue.Amma.Fri2: We keep the trail clear around the shelter entrance.
dialogue.Amma.Sat2: A gust can hide a marker in seconds. We do not race it.
dialogue.Amma.Sun2: I dry the blankets before they go back in the sled box.
dialogue.Amma.Mon4: The dogs work as a team, and rest as a team too.
dialogue.Amma.Tue4: There is always time to check a strap twice.
dialogue.Amma.Wed4: I keep the first aid roll beside the spare line.
dialogue.Amma.Thu4: The camp is a stopping place, not a shortcut across the ice.
dialogue.Amma.Fri4: Thank you for leaving the trail as clear as you found it.
dialogue.Amma.Sat4: Good journeys end with every member of the team safe.

machine.drying.name: Fish drying rack
machine.drying.description: Air-dries one cod or capelin over two nights. No fuel needed. Keeps the fish quality.
product.AtlanticCod.name: Air-dried Atlantic cod
product.AtlanticCod.description: Carefully air-dried at the harbor. A compact, savory fish product.
product.Capelin.name: Air-dried capelin
product.Capelin.description: Carefully air-dried at the harbor. A compact, savory fish product.
product.PolarCod.name: Air-dried polar cod
product.PolarCod.description: Carefully air-dried at the harbor. A compact, savory fish product.
machine.drying.invalid: Use one Atlantic cod, polar cod or capelin.
mail.drying: The shed is ready for slow work, too.^Here is the plan for a fish drying rack. Use 40 wood, 15 fiber and one iron bar. One cod or capelin takes two nights without coal. It keeps the quality of your catch.^-Roan %item craftingRecipe ArcticPassage_DryingRack %%[#]A place to hang the catch
quest.Arrival.title: A northern welcome
quest.Arrival.desc: Yueyueniao has invited you to explore the Arctic. After landing, follow the marked path down to the red guesthouse in Frosthavn.
quest.Arrival.hint: Enter the red guesthouse west of the square.
quest.catch.reply: Fresh and carefully packed. Let us fix the shed next.
quest.FirstCatch_spring.title: The first shipment
quest.FirstCatch_spring.desc: Ada needs three Capelin. This order has no deadline.
quest.FirstCatch_spring.hint: Give Ada 3 Capelin in a single stack.
quest.FirstCatch_summer.title: The first shipment
quest.FirstCatch_summer.desc: Ada needs three Capelin. This order has no deadline.
quest.FirstCatch_summer.hint: Give Ada 3 Capelin in a single stack.
quest.FirstCatch_fall.title: The first shipment
quest.FirstCatch_fall.desc: Ada needs three Atlantic cod. This order has no deadline.
quest.FirstCatch_fall.hint: Give Ada 3 Atlantic cod in a single stack.
quest.FirstCatch_winter.title: The first shipment
quest.FirstCatch_winter.desc: Ada needs three Polar cod. This order has no deadline.
quest.FirstCatch_winter.hint: Give Ada 3 Polar cod in a single stack.
quest.shed.reply: Good boards. The shed will be ready in the morning.
quest.Shed.title: The old processing shed
quest.Shed.desc: Roan needs wood for the shed. He will finish the work overnight.
quest.Shed.hint: Give Roan 40 wood in one stack.
quest.boat.reply: I will finish the fittings tonight. Check the pier sign tomorrow.
quest.BoatRepair.title: A route beyond the harbor
quest.BoatRepair.desc: Two iron bars will secure the old boat. The route opens the next morning.
quest.BoatRepair.hint: Give Roan 2 iron bars in one stack.
quest.FjordVisit.title: Among the icebergs
quest.FjordVisit.desc: The repaired boat runs a fixed route to the observation landing.
quest.FjordVisit.hint: Use the route sign at the east end of the harbor pier.
quest.deep.reply: Our first shipment is complete. There will be more orders tomorrow.
quest.DeepCatch.title: The deep-water catch
quest.DeepCatch.desc: Ada would like one Greenland halibut from the fjord. Fishing level 4 is required.
mail.invitation: Dear farmer,^I am Yueyueniao. Come north with me, beyond the familiar fields, to glacier-carved fjords, wind-swept tundra, and a little town with warm windows: Frosthavn.^Enclosed is a return ticket with Moonbird Air. Check in at our Valley bus-stop transfer point; press B there to view your ticket. Bring your curiosity, and perhaps a fishing rod.^There is no need to rush. Listen to the wind. Watch the Arctic light. I look forward to the stories you bring home.^-Yueyueniao %item object ArcticPassage_FlightTicket 1 %%[#]A ticket to the northern light
mail.processing: The shed is ready.^Here is a Fish Smoker to get started. Ten coal will be delivered when you next arrive in the bay. It uses the normal recipe and professions.^-Roan %item bigobject FishSmoker %%[#]Processing shed ready
mail.route: The boat is ready.^Use the route post at the east end of the harbor pier. The return post is always available on the landing.^-Roan[#]Fjord route open
order.Regular.name: Regular order receipt
order.Regular.desc: Trade the requested fish. Gold payment is added immediately; one delivery per day.
order.Restaurant.name: Restaurant order · silver+
order.Restaurant.desc: Deliver 2 seasonal fish of silver quality or better. Silver fish are used first. Premium payment is immediate; Mira gains 25 friendship. Once per day.
order.Research.name: Research order receipt
order.Research.desc: Deliver 1 seasonal fish of any quality. Payment is immediate and the first delivered sample of this species is recorded. Once per day.
shop.orders: Daily deliveries: regular orders accept 3 seasonal fish of any quality; the guesthouse needs 2 silver-or-better fish and thanks you with Mira friendship; research records 1 sample. Each type can be delivered once per day.
fish.NorthernShrimp.name: Northern shrimp
fish.NorthernShrimp.description: Pandalus borealis. Lives over cold, soft seabeds; commercial fisheries mainly use deep-water trawls. Shore pots are a gameplay simplification.
fish.SnowCrab.name: Snow crab
fish.SnowCrab.description: Chionoecetes opilio. A long-legged cold-water crab. Distribution varies between northern seas; this bay uses a composite geography.
meal.CharSoup.name: Arctic char soup
meal.CharSoup.description: A warm harbor meal made with a carefully handled local catch.
meal.PanCod.name: Pan-fried cod
meal.PanCod.description: A warm harbor meal made with a carefully handled local catch.
meal.ShrimpChowder.name: Cream northern shrimp soup
meal.ShrimpChowder.description: A warm harbor meal made with a carefully handled local catch.
meal.FishPotatoStew.name: Fish and potato stew
meal.FishPotatoStew.description: A warm harbor meal made with a carefully handled local catch.
sign.town: FROSTHAVN — Red house: guesthouse. Blue house: fishery. North: tundra. East: harbor. The return post is beside the east pier. The harbor supply counter sells four cooking recipes and imported staples; the guesthouse kitchen counter is shared. Press K for routes, your next step and nature notes.
sign.inn: Guesthouse entrance: the red front door. Beds are inside.
sign.boat: Fjord route closed for repairs. Finish Roan's wood and iron-bar requests; the boat reopens the next morning.
sign.fishing: Safe fishing from the piers. Spring: capelin and polar cod. Summer and fall: Atlantic cod. Winter: polar cod; cast west from the upper pier into dark open water. Wolffish prefer the northern rocky inlet outside winter. Harbor pots: northern shrimp in spring, summer and fall. Fjord pots: snow crab in fall. In winter use harbor pots for snow crab; the fjord landing is icebound. Bait, leave overnight, and collect from shore.
sign.workshop: Processing shed: ask Roan about repairing it. Wood first, then two iron bars for the boat.
sign.ready: The shed is ready. Roan sent a Fish Smoker and a drying-rack plan. Smoking is quick and needs coal; drying takes two nights without fuel.
sign.deep: Deep-water observation pier. Greenland halibut: all seasons, fishing level 4+. Golden redfish: summer and fall, fishing level 2+. In winter cast south from the viewing platform into dark open water. Icebergs and shore ice cannot be walked on.
sign.whale: The lookout faces the open fjord. Dark water and the blue edges of distant ice fill the view.
sign.tundra: Low shrubs, stones and meltwater. The stream supports Arctic char in summer and fall. South: town. Cross the eastern wooden bridge to reach the field camp and research shelter.
sign.camp.route: Field camp. West: tundra bridge, then south to Frosthavn. The red research hut has a bed on the left. The marked route stays open throughout the year. Enter: continue.
sign.camp.snow: These are seasonal demonstration shelters: snow houses in winter, canvas tents during the other seasons. The red hut is the overnight shelter; the domes are for viewing from the marked path. Enter: continue.
sign.camp.desk: Field research shelter. The bed to the left uses normal overnight saving. Return through the south door, walk west to the bridge, then south to town. K opens your route book and field notes. Enter: continue.
sign.char: Fresh-water channel. Cast from the bridge for Arctic char in summer and fall.
sign.safety: North winds can erase old tracks. Follow the shore markers home, and keep clear of newly formed sea ice.
sign.lodging: The fire is warm; your room is on the left. The shuttle post by the eastern town pier takes you back to the snowfield airstrip. Press B there for your return flight.
event.arrival1: Welcome to Frosthavn! Yueyueniao told us you were flying in. There is a room waiting in the red house; come warm up.
event.arrival2: Bring your rod to the harbor. A few well-kept fish will get our first shipment started. Press K for routes, your next step and nature notes.
event.Ada.personal.1: The ledger says the first crate stayed cold from pier to counter. That small detail is how a harbor earns trust.
event.Ada.personal.2: You kept the label facing out and the drain clear. I will put your name beside this morning’s careful work.
event.Mira.personal.1: The tracks cross the marked path and disappear among the stones. We can learn from them without following or feeding the animal.
event.Mira.personal.2: You left the stones where they were. That is good field practice; the next thaw may tell us more.
event.Roan.personal.1: The harbor lamp was loose in its bracket. I tightened it before dusk; a small light matters when the landing is hard to see.
event.Roan.personal.2: You held the ladder steady and kept the pier clear. That is good repair work, even without a wrench in your hand.
event.Nora.personal.1: The wind sock has gone still, but I still check the ice haze before clearing a flight. A safe return is part of every departure.
event.Nora.personal.2: You noticed the thin line of open water on my chart. Good eyes. I will mark it before the evening report.
event.Levin.personal.1: I drew the ice edge from solid ground and marked where the view was uncertain. A careful record should leave room for what we do not know.
event.Levin.personal.2: You spotted the same ridge in the meltwater sketch. I will add your observation to the field notes, with your name beside it.
event.Amma.personal.1: Before a run, I check each paw, buckle and line. The team sets the pace; if one dog is tired, we all turn back.
event.Amma.personal.2: You held the loose line clear of the path. Thank you. Everyone gets water and a quiet rest before we go out again.
flight.ticket.name: Moonbird Air return ticket
flight.ticket.desc: Destination: Frosthavn. An invitation to explore the Arctic. Press B at the bus stop to check in. Return included; the ticket is not consumed.
flight.airport: Moonbird Air / Frosthavn snowfield airstrip. Follow the marked path south into town; the red guesthouse has a bed. B checks in for your included return. This snowfield sits above the town. Stay off the runway.

r01.workshop: Give Roan 40 wood; the shed opens the next morning. For the boat, the supplies counter offers two iron bars per visitor: each costs 3 seasonal fish (capelin in spring/summer, cod in fall, polar cod in winter). This local contribution never restocks. Imported bars still cost 1000g; home-mined materials also work. Mail is forwarded to the guesthouse desk.
r01.opening.1: Last nail, last check. These boards should stand up to salt and wind.
r01.opening.2: A smoker for quick batches, a rack for slow drying. I sent the equipment and plans to your mail. The guesthouse desk will have them.
r01.opening.3: Keep the walkway clear. A working harbor needs room for everyone.
frontier.sled: Marked mountain trail. South: tundra lookout. North: glacier observation deck. East: field camp. In summer use the gravel walking route. Winter dog-team services operate from the marked station. Never leave the trail to cross sea ice.
frontier.glacier: Observe from this fixed deck. The ice front, crevasses and meltwater channel are out of bounds. Survey stakes measure positions; they do not indicate safe ice. Return south along the marked moraine path.
frontier.geology: The mixed stones at this moraine were carried by moving ice. Survey from the path; never hammer the glacier.
frontier.sled.pending: The dog-team station is being prepared. Follow the marked walking trail for now.
frontier.community: Frosthavn community house. Shared tables, local notices and a kitchen on the right. The south door returns to the upper town lane.
weekly.CoastalLog.name: A week along the coast
weekly.CoastalLog.desc: Catch six northern rod fish before Sunday ends. Only catches made after accepting count. Keep the fish for sale or processing. —Ada
weekly.CoastalLog.objective: Catch 6 northern rod fish after accepting.
weekly.FreshCrates.name: The guesthouse fish crate
weekly.FreshCrates.desc: Put six northern rod fish in the crate below the community noticeboard before Sunday ends. Any species, quality or mixture is accepted; partial deliveries are kept. Confirm by closing the crate. —Ada
weekly.FreshCrates.objective: Put 6 northern rod fish in the community fish crate.
story.order.supplies.name: Gale-ready community stores
story.order.supplies.desc: The community team needs 20 fiber for spare lashings before the next gale. Donate it to the shared box below the noticeboard.
story.order.supplies.objective: Donate 20 fiber to the community supply box.
story.order.fish.name: Fresh catch before the gale
story.order.fish.desc: Ada needs one fresh northern rod fish for the community kitchen. Only a catch made after accepting this order counts.
story.order.fish.objective: Catch one northern rod fish after accepting.
sled.season: The dog-team route opens in winter. Marked walking trails remain open in other seasons.
sled.single: Dog-team travel is currently available in single-player. Please use the marked walking trail in multiplayer.
sled.locked: Mira: Help the harbor repair the processing shed first; then we can prepare the winter route together.
sled.tools: Mira: My lashing tool was left beside the parked sled on the mountain trail. Check the station marker there, then bring it to the tundra stop.
sled.toolFound: You found the lashing tool. Return it at the tundra stop.
sled.toolsDone: The equipment yard is in order. Use the tundra, camp or glacier stop to arrange a journey.
sled.supplies: Mira: Thank you. Collect the packed supplies at the field-camp sign and bring them back to the tundra stop.
sled.supplyFound: The packed supplies are in your bag. Bring them to the tundra stop.
sled.repair: Mira: The last job is the stop repair. Bring 20 wood and 5 fiber to the tundra stop for the rail and lashings.
sled.repairConfirm: Use 20 wood and 5 fiber to repair the tundra stop?
sled.trial: Mira: Everything is checked. Take the first route from the tundra stop to the field camp; then all three winter stops will open.
sled.choose: Mira: The team is ready. Where shall we go?
sled.full: Please leave one empty bag slot for the equipment.
sled.unavailable: The route is not ready. You can still return by the marked walking trail.
sled.unlocked: First journey completed. All three winter dog-team stops are open.
sled.item.0.name: Lashing tool
sled.item.0.desc: Mira left it beside the parked sled. Return it at the tundra stop.
sled.item.1.name: Packed trail supplies
sled.item.1.desc: Packed at the field camp. Deliver it to the tundra stop.

research.reward.name: Field-atlas display
research.reward.desc: A small framed chart made from the harbor team's field notes. Place it indoors as a record of patient observation.
mail.researchReward: Your records are complete.^The catch log, field samples and careful views of the coast now form a useful atlas. I made this small display for the guesthouse or your home. Thank you for looking without disturbing the wildlife.^-Levin %item bigobject ArcticPassage_FieldAtlasDisplay %%[#]A field atlas for Frosthavn
secret.shipModel.name: Old harbor boat model
secret.shipModel.desc: A small wooden keepsake of the old Greenland crossing. A reminder of a route once kept by hand.
mail.oldShipModel: I found this model in my grandfather's chart chest. The old boat kept close to the ice and carried more stories than cargo. I thought you should have it.^-Roan %item bigobject ArcticPassage_OldShipModel %%[#]The old crossing
festival.spring.dialogue.Ada: The first spring catch tells us how the ice is changing.
festival.spring.dialogue.Mira: I've made a small pot of fish-and-potato stew for the pier.
festival.spring.dialogue.Roan: A good cast begins with watching the water, not rushing it.
festival.spring.dialogue.Nora: The prize is small. The stories from the first catch last longer.
festival.spring.dialogue.Levin: We'll note the weight, then return the fish to the cold water.
festival.spring.dialogue.Amma: The wind is kind today. Keep the line clear of the working boats.
festival.reward.spring.name: Harbor knot keepsake
festival.reward.spring.desc: A carefully dressed fishing float tied with the harbor's red signal cord.
festival.spring.name: Harbor Opening Day
festival.spring.started: Harbor Opening Day is underway. Join the fishing challenge, guess a catch, or try today's soup (F).
festival.summer.dialogue.Ada: At this hour, the low sun still reaches the ice beyond the bay.
festival.summer.dialogue.Mira: There is room at the picnic blanket. Take a cup before the walk.
festival.summer.dialogue.Roan: The birds are feeding beyond the outer ice. We watch from shore.
festival.summer.dialogue.Nora: No flash near the nesting ledges, please. A quiet view is enough.
festival.summer.dialogue.Levin: The midnight sun is a season, not a change to the clock.
festival.summer.dialogue.Amma: The dogs have shade and water. We'll keep the path open.
festival.reward.summer.name: Midnight sun horizon
festival.reward.summer.desc: A small painted horizon keeps the pale summer light above the fjord.
festival.summer.name: Midnight Sun Bay Day
festival.summer.started: Midnight Sun Bay Day is bright along the fjord. Press F to join a nature quiz or watch the seabirds.
festival.winter.dialogue.Ada: The lamps are low and warm. We keep the dark sky visible above them.
festival.winter.dialogue.Mira: The soup is ready. There is enough for everyone who made the walk.
festival.winter.dialogue.Roan: The harbor lights help boats find the safe edge of the ice.
festival.winter.dialogue.Nora: Leave one lantern unlit for the stars and the aurora, if it comes.
festival.winter.dialogue.Levin: On clear nights, look north. On rough nights, the warm windows are enough.
festival.winter.dialogue.Amma: The dogs are resting indoors tonight. Let the snow path stay quiet.
festival.reward.winter.name: Frosted harbor lantern
festival.reward.winter.desc: A sheltered lantern with a frosted shade, made for a winter window.
festival.winter.name: Polar Night Lantern Walk
festival.winter.started: The Polar Night Lantern Walk has begun. Press F to share soup, exchange a wish, or watch the winter sky.
story.report.name: Field report packet
story.report.desc: Levin's compiled packet of verified wildlife, landform, and marine observations.
story.mail.field: Your field notes line up.^Three distinct animal records, a landform marker, and a distant marine observation make a useful first survey. Please bring this packet to the research station so I can check the details.^-Levin %item object ArcticPassage_FieldReport %%[#]A record from the coast
story.mail.finale: The fjord order is complete.^The harbor is working again, the field notes are safe, and the town has a route through the winter. Nora would like to see you in the square when you are ready. The fishery, observations, sled trail, and daily orders will stay open.^-Nora[#]A new season in Frosthavn
story.mail.iceModel: You took the time to learn how the camp's snow blocks fit together, then waited for safe ice before fishing. Amma made this small snow-house study model for your room. The ice opening is a fixed fishing site; keep to the marked platform.^-Amma %item bigobject ArcticPassage_IceShelterModel %%[#]A study from the winter camp
story.iceModel.name: Snow-house study model
story.iceModel.desc: A small model of the camp's carefully fitted snow blocks. Indoor display.
story.mail.windbreak: You checked the marked route with Mira and left enough room for the dogs and the weather to set the pace. She built this small windbreak screen for the guesthouse entry. Keep the trail clear and turn back when visibility falls.^-Mira %item bigobject ArcticPassage_WindbreakScreen %%[#]A safer way through the wind
story.windbreak.name: Trail windbreak screen
story.windbreak.desc: A small slatted entry screen inspired by the camp's marked safe route. Indoor display.
story.quest.FieldReport.title: Chapter 6 · Northern field notes
story.quest.FieldReport.desc: Levin can turn the verified observations into a shared field record.
story.quest.FieldReport.hint: Record three animal types, one landform and the distant whale; collect the mailed field packet and deliver it to Levin.
story.quest.FieldReport.reply: These are careful observations. I'll add them to the coast record.
story.quest.StormReadiness.title: Chapter 7 · Before the first gale
story.quest.StormReadiness.desc: The community house is coordinating supplies and a fresh-catch order before the next rough-weather window.
story.quest.StormReadiness.hint: Meet the harbor team at the community house to open its storm-supply board.
story.quest.StormReadiness.reply: We can prepare together before the weather changes. The community box is ready for the team's fiber order.
story.quest.StormSupplies.title: Chapter 7 · Community storm supplies
story.quest.StormSupplies.desc: The harbor team needs spare fiber lashings stored at the community house before the gale.
story.quest.StormSupplies.hint: Accept and complete the one-time storm-supply order at the community board; donate 20 fiber to its box.
story.quest.StormSupplies.reply: The emergency lashings are in place. Ada has opened a fresh-catch order for the harbor kitchen.
story.quest.StormFish.title: Chapter 7 · Fresh catch for the gale
story.quest.StormFish.desc: Ada needs a fresh northern fish for the community kitchen. Only a catch made after taking the order counts.
story.quest.StormFish.hint: Accept the emergency fish order, then make one real northern rod catch.
story.quest.StormFish.reply: The fresh catch is recorded. Mira will walk the marked route with you before the next departure.
story.quest.StormRoute.title: Chapter 7 · Walk the safe route
story.quest.StormRoute.desc: Mira is waiting on the tundra edge to check the wind markers and the clear return path.
story.quest.StormRoute.hint: Speak to Mira on the tundra trail, normally between 11:00 and 15:00, to confirm the marked return route.
story.quest.StormRoute.reply: The route is marked and the return path stays open. Please turn back if visibility drops.
story.quest.CampVisit.title: Chapter 8 · The winter field camp
story.quest.CampVisit.desc: Visit the field camp with Mira. In winter use the dog team; marked walking returns stay open.
story.quest.CampVisit.hint: Reach the ArcticPassage field camp and read the shelter and ice-safety signs.
story.quest.CampVisit.reply: The camp is ready for a quiet visit. The marked ice hole is only fished from its timber platform.
story.quest.ShelterLesson.title: Chapter 8 · Fit the snow blocks
story.quest.ShelterLesson.desc: Use Amma's winter camp model to learn the offset courses used by a snow shelter.
story.quest.ShelterLesson.hint: Complete all three courses at the snow-house model in the winter field camp.
story.quest.ShelterLesson.reply: The courses are stable and the entrance stays clear. When the marked fjord opening is prepared, fish only from its timber deck.
story.quest.IceCatch.title: Chapter 8 · Fish from the marked ice opening
story.quest.IceCatch.desc: The camp lesson is complete. On a winter day, clear the surveyed opening beside the fjord platform and make one real rod catch there.
story.quest.IceCatch.hint: Make one ordinary rod catch in the open ice hole at the Icefjord; stay on the timber platform.
story.quest.IceCatch.reply: A careful lesson and a real catch make a good winter record. Amma has sent you a small snow-house study model.
story.quest.DriedOrder.title: Chapter 9 · A farther harbor order
story.quest.DriedOrder.desc: Air-dry a cod or capelin at the harbor rack, then make the first export trade at Ada's order counter.
story.quest.DriedOrder.hint: Trade one air-dried Atlantic cod, polar cod, or capelin for the first export receipt at the order counter.
story.quest.DriedOrder.reply: The export route is working. Daily processed-fish trades and the weekly export order are now open.
story.quest.WarmHarbor.title: Chapter 10 · A new season
story.quest.WarmHarbor.desc: The team is gathering to remember the winter harbor in a lantern-lit tableau. Your actual game date and season are preserved.
story.quest.WarmHarbor.hint: Enter the town between 18:00 and midnight to join the six residents' lantern finale.
story.quest.WarmHarbor.reply: We made it through the season together. Tomorrow the boats, field notes, and daily work continue.
story.trade.first.name: First export receipt
story.trade.daily.name: Harbor export receipt
story.trade.desc: The counter has received the processed fish and paid directly into your wallet.
story.routeConfirm: The return markers are clear and the trail stays on firm ground. Keep the wind at your side, leave room for the dog team, and turn back before visibility closes. I'll keep checking the route with you.
story.export.name: A box for the next crossing
story.export.desc: The harbor's new buyer needs four air-dried fish this week. Donate them at the shared community box. —Ada
story.export.objective: Donate four air-dried northern fish for export.
story.finale.nora: The last lantern post is ready. Tonight we can leave work for a moment and remember the winter light that brought us together.
story.finale.roan: The boat has a sound hull again. Beyond the warm windows, the next crossing is waiting.
story.finale.ada: Your catches, careful drying and first export have given the harbor a new rhythm. There will be work here tomorrow.
story.finale.mira: And a marked way home. If the wind rises, the journey can wait.
story.finale.levin: We learned to watch quietly: the ice, the birds, and the light moving above us.
story.finale.amma: The team is resting. The soup is warm. Stay with us until the lanterns settle.
story.finale.end: Frosthavn is part of your story now. Boats, trails, nature notes and harbor orders remain open whenever you return.
story.quest.MultiWaterCatch.title: Chapter 9 · Two waters, one harbor
story.quest.MultiWaterCatch.desc: The new buyer wants to understand the coast and inland waters before opening the longer route.
story.quest.MultiWaterCatch.hint: Catch and keep one rod fish in each of two different waters: harbor, Icefjord, or tundra stream.
story.quest.MultiWaterCatch.reply: Two waters are now represented. Prepare a dried fish for the first export trade.
story.quest.FinalePreparation.title: Chapter 10 · Posts for the lanterns
story.quest.FinalePreparation.desc: Nora is preparing the harbor team's lantern gathering. The celebration can take place without waiting for the annual festival.
story.quest.FinalePreparation.hint: Bring 10 wood to Nora for the lantern posts.
story.quest.FinalePreparation.reply: The lantern posts are ready. Come into town between 18:00 and midnight for our winter-night tableau.
